key_insight: TrajectoryFlowNet learns both how particles move and how fluid flows from very limited trajectory measurements. Its physics-informed approach connects individual particle paths with the surrounding flow field.
problem_solved: Reconstructing flow fields and predicting long-range particle trajectories when only sparse particle-motion measurements are available.
method: Combines Lagrangian learning of particle trajectories with Eulerian learning of flow fields.
Uses physics-informed learning to jointly predict long-range particle paths and fluid motion from limited trajectory data.
Evaluates the approach in simulations and blood-flow experiments.
impact: This work illustrates how physical constraints can support learning from sparse measurements. It offers a promising approach for practitioners developing models for fluid dynamics and biomedical flow analysis.
visual_elements: Sparse measured particle positions transitioning into predicted continuous trajectories.
A side-by-side diagram linking particle-following Lagrangian and fixed-location Eulerian views.
A flow-field map with particle paths overlaid to illustrate joint prediction.
Paired simulation and blood-flow experiment panels highlighting the validation settings.
paper_title: Lagrangian–Eulerian learning of flow field and trajectories with TrajectoryFlowNet
paper_authors: Jingdi Wan, Hongping Wang, Bo Liu, Xiaolei Yang, Xiaodong Hu
